newsitem.title: UK: UK's Labour commits to review of government assets.
newsitem.headline: UK's Labour commits to review of government assets.

text.p: Britain's opposition Labour Party, launching its business manifesto on Friday, committed itself to a review of all government assets with a view to selling some off.
"We will instruct all government departments to compile registers of the assets they own by the end of this year," said Gordon Brown, Labour's finance spokesman.
Labour's manifesto said if it was decided there was no need for departments to hold property, land or other assets, they will be required to sell them.

The manifesto said the old argument as to whether pubic ownership or privatisation was best is no longer relevant. It pledged to continue public/private partnerships through the Private Finance Initiative, which seeks to lure private cash into public infrastructure projects.
"Deals already signed or accepted as operationally and financially viable will proceed without delay," the manifesto said. -- London Newsroom +44 171 542 7715
